Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

madness noun

also insanity, lunacy, frenzy, folly

classical

Plaut. Amph. 798: jam tū quoque hujus adjuvās īnsāniam?
Cic. Tusc. 3.8: nōmen īnsāniae significat mentis aegrōtātiōnem et morbum (Lewis & Short)

īnsānia, īnsāniae f.

noun, first declension

unsoundness of mind, madness; mad folly

Other words

  • āmentia, āmentiae f. — being out of one’s senses, madness

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.10: animī adfectiōnem lūmine mentis carentem nōmināvērunt āmentiam eandemque dēmentiam (Lewis & Short)

  • dēmentia, dēmentiae f. — being out of one’s mind; madness, folly

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.10 (Lewis & Short); Ter. Ad. 4.7.40 (Lewis & Short)

  • rabiēs (rabiem, rabiē) f. — madness (properly of dogs); rage, fury, frenzy

    also used · classical · Liv. 21.48.4: velut injectā rabiē ad arma itūrōs (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ars 79 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Ei mihi, jam tū quoque hujus adjuvās īnsāniam?

    Oh dear, are you too now encouraging her in her madness?Plaut. Amph. 798

  • contāctōs eō scelere velut injectā rabiē ad arma itūrōs

    that, tainted by that crime, they would rush to arms as if a madness had been cast on themLiv. 21.48.4 (Lewis & Short)

See also crazy, be mad, foolishness.
